title: Nightcap continuity digest — cache throttle incident and follow-ups
incident_summary: Between 00:12 and 00:48 UTC we saw sustained 5x increase in inference tail latency for hosted-api region-us-east-1. Root symptom was a spike in cache miss ratio and Redis latency after a progressive config rollout to prefix-cache v2. Upstream autoscaler reacted slowly due to a mis-set scaling window, causing token fanout to hit origin pools and saturate CPU on a subset of pods. No data exfiltration; service remained reachable with degraded latency. No customer-facing outage declared, but several internal throttles and retries elevated error budgets for the night.
body:
Quick notes / narrative:

- 00:06 UTC: Canary rollout of prefix-cache v2 started (config change: LFU->LRU sampling tweak).
- 00:12 UTC: Synthetic latency alert (P95 > 600ms) fires for hosted-api/us-east-1. SRE oncall paged.
- 00:14 UTC: Observed cache miss ratio climb from 8% -> 62% in 10m window; Redis avg cmd latency increased 4x.
- 00:20 UTC: Autoscaler logs show scaling-event suppressed: scaleDownWindow and scaleUpCooldown were set to 10m by mistake in the canary config; HPA target CPU still below threshold for several pods.
- 00:25 UTC: We manually increased replica count for origin-pool-02 (kubectl scale) and restarted cache pods to clear unhealthy client connections.
- 00:34 UTC: Latency begins to stabilize; cache miss ratio drops to ~15% after TTL rehydration and warmed prefixes.
- 00:48 UTC: Alerts return to baseline. Night team kept watch until 02:00 to ensure no recurrence.

What we tried (quick mitigation):
- bump origin-pool-02 replicas from 6->12 (immediate relief for throughput)
- rolling restart of prefix-cache deployment to flush stale client session multiplexing
- enabled emergency fallback routing: route small-batch requests to quantized-model-128 when prefix cache miss rate > 40% (temporary policy)
- applied hotfix to HPA config in staging then promoted to canary to remove the 10m cooldown misconfig

Commands run (notes to ops):
- kubectl scale deployment/origin-pool-02 -n hosted-api --replicas=12
- kubectl rollout restart deployment/prefix-cache -n hosted-api
- curl -X POST https://internal-routing/override -d '{"policy":"fallback-quant128"}' (internal auth)

Observations / metrics of interest (until 02:00 UTC):
- Redis p99 cmd latency peaked at 320ms (baseline ~60ms)
- origin-pool CPU per-pod jumped to 92% on average for 8 minutes before scaling
- synthetic P95 latency returned to ~220ms after mitigations

Runbook draft (initial thoughts — needs cleanup and owners):
- Detection:
  - Add a composite alert that fires when cache_miss_ratio > 40% AND redis_avg_cmd_latency > 200ms for 5m.
  - Surface HPA suppression events as an alert (scale suppression detected).
- Immediate steps:
  1) Check canary rollout list: which config changed recently? rollback if within last 30m.
  2) If cache_miss_ratio > 50% escalate to SRE oncall and scale origin pools by X (owner: SRE oncall).
  3) If redis_p99 > 250ms, consider forcing prefix-cache restart and enable fallback-routing policy.
- Mitigation knobs:
  - Emergency scale (kubectl scale or API to fleet manager).
  - Prefix-cache soft restart and connection pruning to recover stuck clients.
  - Routing fallback to quantized/low-LR models to reduce CPU per-request.
- Post-incident:
  - Create a PR to fix default HPA cooldowns in the deployment templates.
  - Add a smoke test: local canary that exercises cache warming with representative prefix distributions.

Notes-to-self and scribbles (informal):
- Why did the config change flip cache sampling mechanics and not be gated by a canary size? Need a checklist: config + perf test + smoke warm.
- Investigate whether client libs opened too many persistent connections that survived the rollout and created uneven request routing.
- Possible longer-term: move prefix cache into a StatefulSet with graceful drain logic so we don't get cold-client storms on restarts.

Open questions (for postmortem):
- Which customers saw elevated tail latency the most (map by token prefix)?
- Did any rate limiter token buckets hit limits during the spike?
- Should fallback-routing be automated instead of manual POST? (prefer an autonomous circuit-breaker)

Immediate action items (for next 72h):
- (A1) PR to set HPA default cooldowns to 30s/60s boundaries and add unit tests (owner: @diego).
- (A2) Add composite cache+redis alert with playbook link (owner: @lina).
- (A3) Run a tabletop in next SRE ops sync to rehearse cache-stall scenario (owner: @priya).
- (A4) Draft a small integration test that warms cache during canaries (owner: eng-serving-runtime).

Slack thread notes: #oncall-night posted timeline + temp routing override. Tagging product-api to check any correlated deploys.

If you pick this up next: start by checking the canary rollout history (kubectl rollout history deployment/prefix-cache -n hosted-api) and the HPA events (kubectl describe hpa -n hosted-api). Prioritize A1 and A2.

Short sign-off blurb for whoever relieves me: I patched the HPA cooldown in canary, scaled origin pool, restarted prefix-cache, and left fallback-routing enabled until 03:00 UTC. No regressions observed. Will follow up with a short postmortem draft in the morning. Good luck.
action_items: Tabletop rehearsal for cache-stall (owner: Priya Reddy)
Integration: canary cache-warm test (owner: eng-serving-runtime team)
